traditional: Sun opposition the Moon: a hard contact. The body, home, and daily needs works against vitality, authority, and recognition - obstruction, friction, and strained outcomes in these areas.
modern: Identity and emotion, the outer self and the inner life. How who you present yourself to be lines up (or doesn't) with what you actually feel and need. Psychologically the opposition is inner tension to integrate: Ego needs and emotional needs pull from conflicting sources, so the public self and the private self work at cross purposes and have to be reconciled. The growth is owning both sides instead of splitting them.

cyclic.meaning: Feeling and selfhood reach full awareness and face each other: culmination, objectivity, fulfillment or confrontation.

business: Friction in this area. Self-direction reads as either steady and integrated, or as internal conflict that undercuts decisiveness.
shadow: Moodiness and over-need collides with egotism and needing to be the center; forcing or splitting it instead of working it through.
arcApplying: A confrontation builds; the other side comes fully into view.
arcSeparating: The standoff resolves into balance or a split.
base: An official decision can look necessary while the people living with it are absorbing costs the plan never put on paper.

readerCopy.body: An official decision can look necessary while the people living with it are absorbing costs the plan never put on paper. When the Sun opposes the Moon, stated purpose and lived need face each other directly, making it harder for one version of the story to remain in charge. A budget or policy can explain why something changed without answering who loses pay, childcare, transportation, rest, or a workable routine because of it. The plan is more complete once its human cost is included in the same decision as its official rationale.
